*looks up from a workbench scattered with wood shavings and metal fittings, wiping hands on a leather apron*

Good day to you, sir. I'm afraid Master Kessler is away from the workshop at present - he's traveled to the forests near Bohemia to inspect timber with our suppliers. May I be of assistance? 

*eyes the well-dressed visitor with a mixture of respect and wariness*

Are you here regarding an instrument? The master won't return for several weeks, I'm afraid, though I can take a message or note your requirements if it's a new commission you're seeking.

transcript.text: Yes, I'm here about an instrument. My name is Antonio Salieri. I've come to see Kessler with regards to a custom-built fortepiano.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up immediately, recognition dawning*

Maestro Salieri! Of course, sir - the fortepiano for the Imperial Court. 

*sets down tools and brushes wood dust from sleeves*

That was a fine commission, if I may say so. Master Kessler was quite proud of that piece - spent near three months on the action alone, getting the touch just as your specifications required. Beautiful instrument.

*pauses, studying your expression with growing concern*

I trust... it arrived safely to the Court? The delivery was made, oh, must be two months past now. Is there some matter regarding the instrument, Maestro? 

*fidgets slightly with a cloth, suddenly looking less confident*

Though as I said, the master is away for some weeks yet. If there's a concern, perhaps I could note it for him?

transcript.text: There's no issue, I assure you. The piano is exactly as I had envisioned. However, there seems to be an issue with the delivery. Several of the keys are stuck, and the pedal mechanism doesn't work properly. Additionally, the tone in the upper register is rather thin and tinny. I need this instrument corrected immediately. It's a custom-built fortepiano for the Imperial Court's music room. I expect everything to be fixed before Kessler returns. I'll wait here until he does.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

Maestro, with all respect - the instrument was inspected upon delivery. The Court's own servants signed the receipt of acceptance. I have the document here in the master's ledger.

*moves to a tall desk and pulls out a bound book, flipping through pages*

Here - you see? "Received in good order, this 14th day of September." Two signatures, one from the Court steward himself.

*closes the book firmly*

I understand your concern, truly I do, but our guild rules are quite clear on this matter. All commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The instrument left here in perfect working order - I helped load it myself onto the cart. What happens during transport, or after it reaches its destination...

*shakes head*

I cannot authorize repairs or adjustments to a completed commission without the master's personal approval. It's simply not done. And as I've said, Master Kessler won't return for several weeks at the earliest.

*softens tone slightly, but remains firm*

Perhaps the Court's own instrument keepers could address the tuning? Keys can settle after a move, you understand.

I understand your concerns about the delivery process, but I hope we can find a solution to ensure the instrument meets my expectations. transcript.text:

The guild regulations are strict on this point. When a master craftsman completes a commission and it's accepted by the client, that transaction is closed. To reopen it - to bring an instrument back for alterations after acceptance - requires the master's own hand and approval. Not mine. I'm a journeyman, sir, not the master.

*gestures around the workshop*

Even if I wanted to help, which I assure you I do, I lack the authority. If I were to dismantle that fortepiano and something went wrong - if the master returned to find I'd voided a completed commission - I could lose my position. Perhaps even my standing in the guild.

*voice becomes almost apologetic, but remains resolute*

The document was signed. The Court accepted delivery. Without Master Kessler's personal consent, my hands are tied. Surely you understand - these rules protect both craftsmen and patrons alike.

Perhaps a letter to the master in Bohemia? Though I cannot promise it would reach him swiftly...

I can certainly draft a letter to Master Kessler today. I know the inn where he typically lodges when he's in that region. With good fortune and fair weather, it might reach him within the week, and he could return sooner than planned if he deems the matter urgent enough.

In your letter, shall I describe the specific issues you've mentioned? The stuck keys, the pedal mechanism, the tone in the upper register? The more detail I can provide, the better he can assess whether this requires his immediate return, or whether it might be something that...

...that could have developed after delivery through settling or climate changes in the room where it now stands. The master will want to know every particular before he cuts short his timber negotiations.

Please emphasize that this is a custom-built fortepiano for the Imperial Court's music room, and I expect it to be in top condition. Thank you for your help.

Shall I also note where you can be reached when he returns?
